Messages.Author: Tek Ying
Messages.Body:
I finally had to contest a vampire in the last game of Jyhad that I
played, and I have a game-altering question. My friend/prey, whose vampire
I was contesting, figured that when a vampire is contested, it is
technically uncontrolled, so that you could use two tranfers a turn to
take a blood off of it to your blood pool. I doubt that you can do this...
has there been a ruling? thanks.

tek.

Messages.Author: J Greely
Messages.Body:
In article <338co2$o6m@search01.news.aol.com> tekying@aol.com
 (Tek Ying) writes:
>My friend/prey, whose vampire I was contesting, figured that when a
>vampire is contested, it is technically uncontrolled,

I agree, based on the statement in section 7.1:
	...if two players put the same vampire into play, it is
	considered contested, which means the Methuselahs are
	struggling to control it.

>so that you could use two tranfers a turn to take a blood off of it
>to your blood pool.

No.  Uncontrolled is not synonymous with inactive.  Section 8 says
that the only thing you can do with contested vampires (or contested
cards in general) is pay their upkeep, yield (burn them), or, if there
are no longer any other contesting cards with this name/title, you can
bring it into play at the start of your turn.

  The inactive cards are face-down to hide them from the other
players; the contested cards are face-down to indicate that they are
not under your control.  Since vampires aren't the only thing that can
be contested, and since section 8 does not state that contested
vampires are moved to the inactive region, I say that they are
uncontrolled but not inactive.
--
J Greely (jgreely@synopsys.com)

Also, is there anyway to transfer blood to/from a contested minion? It seems
that given equal holdings the person who places their vamp down last will 
win in the end.

Scott

Unique right, so what happens to cards that say for rest of game?

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Jason Alexander <jalex@u.washington.edu> wrote:
>	Now a quick question that might just pertain...  A vampire is
>Unique right, so what happens to cards that say for rest of game?
>	An example would be Patagia.  Desc. says this vampire... for the 
>rest of the game.  Does that mean that the card transfers if I lose the
>vampire in a contest?  Also, if the vampire dies and someone else brings
>it into play does the card still hold?

In the story behind the game, vampires are unique.  For game purposes,
you equip cards individually, assign retains and Camarillas to them
individually, and so on.  You aren't augmenting the name "Koko" or
whatever, but rather that specific card.  If you drop a contested vampire,
the other copy of that vampire doesn't get any equipment and whatnot
on yours.  If a vampire is burned, everything played on that vampire is
burned, and doesn't carry over to the next "incarnation" of that vampire.


Tom Wylie		rec.games.deckmaster Network Representative for
aahz@hal.com			Wizards of the Coast, Inc.
